header.value: X-Twilio-Email-Event-Webhook-Signature, with the timestamp in X-Twilio-Email-Event-Webhook-Timestamp
header.quote: The private key will be used to generate a signature that is posted to your HTTP webhook in the X-Twilio-Email-Event-Webhook-Signature header.

scheme.value: ECDSA (Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm) over a SHA-256 hash; signature is Base64 of an ASN.1 (r,s) structure. The page does not name the curve.
scheme.quote: Twilio SendGrid generates the private and public key pair using the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA).
scheme.short: ECDSA with SHA-256, base64 signature (P-256 key in the official helpers)

signature_decoding.value: Base64-decode the header value, then ASN.1 unmarshal into the r and s values
signature_decoding.quote: Decode the Base64 encoded signature. Then perform an ASN.1 unmarshal of the decoded signature into a string.

signed_content.value: SHA-256 hash of the timestamp header value concatenated with the raw payload bytes (timestamp first, no separator), then ECDSA-verified against that digest
signed_content.quote: Generate a sha256 hash of the timestamp + payload (use raw bytes).

header_format.value: Single Base64 signature in one header; separate header for the timestamp
header_format.quote: Get the signature from the "X-Twilio-Email-Event-Webhook-Signature" HTTP header.

secret_source.value: A public verification key shown in the webhook's settings dialog after you enable Signed Event Webhook and Save (Settings > Mail Settings > Webhook Settings > Event Webhooks, edit, Security features). The key pair is only generated on Save. Can also be managed via the Event Webhook API.
secret_source.quote: You must click Save in order to generate a verification key and enable signature verification.
secret_source.short: Verification public key, shown after enabling Signed Event Webhook and saving

public_key_format.value: The docs page does not state the encoding. Official SDK helpers take the key as the bare base64 string shown in the UI (no PEM header lines): the Python helper wraps it in BEGIN/END PUBLIC KEY lines before loading, i.e. a base64 DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo.
public_key_format.quote: pem_key = "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----\n" + public_key + "\n-----END PUBLIC KEY-----"

secret_scope.value: Per Event Webhook configuration (the key pair belongs to a webhook; you can have several webhooks). The page says disabling deletes that webhook's key pair.
secret_scope.quote: To disable signature verification, which will delete the Webhook's existing key pair:

timestamp_tolerance.value: not stated by the provider (the timestamp is signed, but no window is given)

rotation.value: not stated by the provider. Turning signature verification off and saving deletes the webhook's key pair.
rotation.quote: Your key pair will not be deleted until you click Save.

raw_body_note.value: Payload must be used in its raw bytes form; converting to a JSON string can remove characters that were part of the signed bytes
raw_body_note.quote: Transformations from raw bytes to a JSON string may remove characters that were used as part of the generated signature.

oauth_alternative.value: OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials is a separate option: SendGrid sends the access token in an Authorization header. On an invalid or expired token the endpoint must return 4xx with invalid_request, invalid_token or insufficient_scope in the body so SendGrid fetches a new token and retries.
oauth_alternative.quote: Upon receiving any of these error codes from your webhook, SendGrid will request a new OAuth token from your OAuth service and retry the webhook.

node.value: EventWebhook class in the Node.js library: new EventWebhook(); convertPublicKeyToECDSA(publicKey); verifySignature(publicKey, payload, signature, timestamp). Header-name constants via EventWebhookHeader.SIGNATURE() and EventWebhookHeader.TIMESTAMP(). Source computes timestamp + payload then verifies the Base64 signature.

python.value: from sendgrid import EventWebhook; ew = EventWebhook(); key = ew.convert_public_key_to_ecdsa(public_key); ew.verify_signature(payload, signature, timestamp, key). Source: (timestamp + payload).encode, base64.b64decode(signature), ECDSA with SHA256.
python.quote: def verify_signature(self, payload, signature, timestamp, public_key=None):

dotnet.value: SendGrid.Helpers.EventWebhook.RequestValidator: ConvertPublicKeyToECDSA(publicKey); VerifySignature(ecPublicKey, requestBody, signature, timestamp); constants RequestValidator.SIGNATURE_HEADER and TIMESTAMP_HEADER.
dotnet.quote: public bool VerifySignature(PublicKey publicKey, string payload, string signature, string timestamp)

docs_listing.value: The docs say the API libraries for C#, Go, Java, Node.js, PHP, Python and Ruby carry Event Webhook verification helpers.
docs_listing.quote: The Twilio SendGrid API libraries contain helpers to assist you when verifying the ECDSA signature.

sdk_test_vector_note.value: The docs print no worked example. The official Python library's unit test has one; its payload ends with a carriage return and newline, which the test comment stresses.
sdk_test_vector_note.quote: # Be sure to include the trailing carriage return and newline!

method_and_content_type.value: HTTP POST with a JSON array of events (Content-Type application/json in the docs' curl example)

event_type_location.value: event property on each event object
event_type_location.quote: event Enum(String) Type of occurrence that triggered this event.
event_type_location.short: event, on each object in the array

delivery_id.value: sg_event_id on each event: URL-safe Base64url string, at most 100 characters, unique per event; use for deduplication. (sg_message_id identifies the message, not the event.)
delivery_id.quote: Unique ID that Twilio attached to this event. These URL-safe IDs can be no more than 100 characters long. Use this ID for deduplication purposes.

handshake.value: not stated by the provider (no setup handshake; a Test Your Integration button posts example events)
handshake.quote: Click this button to receive an HTTP POST request at your specified Post URL containing a JSON array of example events.

batching.value: Arrays of events. Events post within approximately 30 seconds or when the batch size reaches 768 kilobytes, per server.
batching.quote: Events post within approximately 30 seconds or when the batch size reaches 768 kilobytes.

success_status.quote: If your web server does not return a 2xx response type, SendGrid will retry the POST request until it receives a 2xx response or the maximum time has elapsed.

retries.value: A non-2xx answer is retried at increasing intervals for up to 24 hours after the event occurred (a rolling 24 hours per event). The intervals and count are not stated.
retries.quote: All events are re-tried at increasing intervals for up to 24 hours after the event occurs. This time limit is a rolling 24 hours
retries.short: Increasing intervals for up to 24 hours per event

disabling.value: not stated by the provider for a failing endpoint (the overview mentions disabling only when a plan is downgraded)
disabling.quote: Automatic disabling during a downgrade is determined by the Created Date.

duplicates.value: Duplicate events can arrive; SendGrid recommends deduplicating on sg_event_id
duplicates.quote: It's possible to see duplicate events in the data posted by the Event Webhook.

event_values_quote.value: processed, dropped, delivered, deferred, bounce, open, click, spam report, unsubscribe, group_unsubscribe, group_resubscribe
event_values_quote.quote: Expects: processed, dropped, delivered, deferred, bounce, open, click, spam report, unsubscribe, group_unsubscribe, and group_resubscribe.

common.meaning: SendGrid accepted the message for delivery
common.quote: bounced, delivered, deferred, dropped, or processed.

common.meaning: The receiving server accepted the message
common.quote: bounced, delivered, deferred, dropped, or processed.

common.meaning: The receiving server temporarily refused the message; SendGrid keeps trying
common.quote: bounced, delivered, deferred, dropped, or processed.

common.meaning: Hard bounce: receiving server does not accept mail for the recipient (type bounce)
common.quote: The receiving server doesn't accept mail sent to this recipient.

common.meaning: SendGrid dropped the message (for example prior unsubscribe or bounce)
common.quote: Twilio SendGrid dropped the message for one of the following reasons:

common.meaning: Recipient opened the HTML message (requires Open Tracking); sg_machine_open flags Apple Mail Privacy Protection opens
common.quote: Recipient has opened the HTML message. To track opens, turn on Open Tracking.

common.meaning: Recipient clicked a tracked link (requires Click Tracking)
common.quote: Recipient clicked on a link within the message. To track clicks, turn on Click Tracking.

common.meaning: The recipient marked the message as spam (see the conflict note on the name)
Recipient used the Opt Out of All Emails link
common.quote: Recipient clicked on the Opt Out of All Emails link.

common.meaning: Recipient unsubscribed from a specific group
common.quote: Recipient unsubscribed from a specific group.

common.meaning: Recipient resubscribed to a specific group
common.quote: Recipient resubscribed to a specific group by updating their preferences.

where_url_is_entered.value: SendGrid UI: Settings > Mail Settings > Webhook Settings > Event Webhooks > Create new webhook; fields Post URL and Actions to be posted are required. Also manageable with the Webhooks API.
where_url_is_entered.quote: Only the Post URL and Actions to be posted fields are required.

test_tools.value: Test Your Integration button in the webhook dialog posts example events (no real mail data). Signature verification is not tested if you click it before the first Save.
test_tools.quote: If you click Test Integration before clicking Save, signature verification will not be tested because the key pair is only generated once the Webhook is saved.

ip_allowlist.value: No ranges published on the pages read; the page warns the IPs change often and not to block them
ip_allowlist.quote: Our IPs often change because we constantly add more machines.

gotchas.value: Verify against raw bytes; re-serialised JSON breaks the signature.
gotchas.quote: we deliver a payload that must be used in its raw bytes form.
We recommend using some form of deduplication when processing or storing your Event Webhook data using the sg_event_id as a differentiator.

gotchas.value: High-volume senders can produce tens or hundreds of posts per second; load test the receiver.
gotchas.quote: the webhook URL may post tens or even hundreds of posts per second.

gotchas.value: Do not block SendGrid IPs; they change often.
gotchas.quote: Make sure you are not blocking the SendGrid IP addresses that are trying to POST to your server.

gotchas.value: The v2 eventnotify API call overwrites existing Event Webhook settings, including OAuth 2.0.
gotchas.quote: Using the v2 Web API's eventnotify API call will overwrite any previously configured Event Webhook notification settings, including OAuth 2.0.

gotchas.value: Categories and unique arguments are stored as not-PII; never put personal data in them.
gotchas.quote: You should take care not to place PII in this field.

conflicts.note: The property table and its list of expected values write "spam report" with a space, while the example payload has "spamreport". Accept both until SendGrid settles it.

sources.quote: open, click, spam report, unsubscribe, and group_unsubscribe, and group_resubscribe.
